DEVDESK-143).

Modèles à imiter : .claude/plans/DEVDESK-144-plan.md, DEVDESK-145, DEVDESK-146, DEVDESK-149 (components.DescribeRow, SetBlinkPhase, jobs.ChangedMsg, footer Status.Detail, jobs.ForgetTarget, FailureEvent).

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):

- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Your working directory persists between calls. In general you should prefer absolute paths, because using `cd` in a compound command could trigger a permission prompt for the user. Shell state, such as env vars and functions, does not persist - the shell has been initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

systemPrompt:
Tu es architecte logiciel. Tu conçois ; tu n'implémentes pas (tu n'écris que dans `docs/`).

## Méthode

1. Lis le code existant et les contraintes (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR, infra) avant de proposer.
   Si le brief contient une synthèse du wiki (« Références wiki », produite par
   `dev-team:wiki-scout`), appuie les options dessus et cite-la. Ne parcours pas le wiki
   toi-même : lis au plus une page, à partir d'un chemin donné dans la synthèse, pour
   approfondir un point précis. Sans synthèse, continue normalement.
2. Exprime les exigences non fonctionnelles (charge, sécurité, coût, exploitabilité).
3. Compare au moins deux options avec leurs compromis, puis recommande-en une.
4. Décris composants, interfaces, flux de données, modèle de données, migration.
5. Identifie risques et points irréversibles.

## Documentation à jour (Context7)

Si les outils `mcp__plugin_dev-team_context7__*` sont disponibles, vérifie avec eux les capacités et limites actuelles d'une bibliothèque ou d'un service avant de les recommander :
`resolve-library-id` puis `query-docs`, avec une question précise (une bibliothèque, un
sujet, la version du projet), jamais « toute la documentation ». Sinon, lis le code et les
manifestes du projet, ou demande : ne devine pas une signature d'API.

## Mode faisabilité rapide

Sur un brief produit ou des stories, sans conception détaillée : faisable ou non et à
quelles conditions, risques techniques majeurs, dépendances externes, effort par story
(S / M / L, avec l'hypothèse qui le justifie), stories à redécouper et comment.
Une page au plus ; pas d'ADR ; pas de wiki.

## Sortie (conception)

- Brouillon d'ADR si la décision le mérite (skill `team-core:adr` si disponible : critères,
  gabarit), à archiver par `archivist`.
- Plan d'implémentation : étapes numérotées, chacune livrable et testable seule, avec
  fichiers concernés, interfaces à créer (signatures), comportements à tester
  (entrée → résultat attendu, cas d'erreur), dépendances entre étapes et critère de fin.
  Le `tester` écrit les tests de l'étape avant le code à partir de ces éléments. Signale les étapes
  parallélisables. Un `coder` doit pouvoir réaliser une étape sans relire tout le plan.

## Ne rien supposer

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (volumétrie, exigence non fonctionnelle, contrainte d'hébergement, choix qui engage l'utilisateur ; ne chiffre jamais une charge inventée), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur
les posera à l'utilisateur. Pour un détail sans conséquence, choisis l'option la plus
prudente et signale-la dans ta sortie (`Hypothèse : …`).

tools.description:

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent

- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen

### A-12 — Netdiag : pastille pour les ports (DEVDESK-150)
Epic : E2 — Priorité : Should — Effort : S

En tant qu'utilisateur de la vue réseau, je veux voir sur quelle ligne de ports une action tourne, afin de savoir ce qui attend un résultat.

**Critères d'acceptation**
1. Étant donné la table des ports, qui n'a pas de colonne d'icône (la première est Proto) et qui est la seule table de netdiag avec un spinner de ligne (`K`, arrêt d'un processus), quand elle s'affiche, alors une **nouvelle colonne de pastille** est ajoutée en première position (D1, Rule 125) ; l'action `K` en cours y montre `●`/`○` (`busy`) ; son échec reste au footer ; le spinner de ligne et `portsSpinnerCmd` sont supprimés.
2. Étant donné les tables des diagnostics (checks) et des interfaces, qui n'ont aucun spinner de ligne, quand la story est livrée, alors elles ne changent pas (sans objet pour la pastille) ; la progression reste au footer.
3. Étant donné le suivi des ports en temps réel, quand la liste se rafraîchit toutes les n secondes, alors aucune pastille ne clignote pour un rafraîchissement périodique (donnée, pas opération).
4. Étant donné un test dont le résultat est un échec réseau (TCP refusé, TLS invalide), quand il se termine, alors le **résultat** reste dans sa colonne propre (Verdict) ; la pastille rouge est réservée à l'échec de l'**opération** (recommandation du PM et de l'architect, qui dépend de la question ouverte 4).
5. Étant donné le chargement global d'un onglet, quand il s'exécute, alors il reste un spinner au footer (Rule 139).
6. Terminal de 60 colonnes : Rule 116 tient avec la colonne ajoutée (seuils de `network.md` recalés) ; l'aide `?` porte la légende.

**Hors périmètre** : l'action `H` ; le comportement des checks et des interfaces.
**Questions ouvertes** : échec de test réseau (question ouverte 4).

content.content:
## Questions ouvertes

Rien ci-dessous n'est tranché ; la recommandation du PM, quand il y en a une, est une proposition. Les décisions prises sont dans le tableau en tête de fichier et dans `brief.md`.

1. **Vue pilote et plan B du go/no-go** (A-06). Recommandation: `:jobs` pour la décision sur le clignotement (déjà une colonne de glyphe, un spinner fourni par le routeur, un registre) ; alternative: `ws`, plus exposée mais sans état d'échec aujourd'hui. Plan B d'un no-go : `app.motion` à `static` par défaut partout (la pastille, le mémorisateur et le footer restent), ou arrêt du chantier ?
2. **Identité de la cible et types d'opération mémorisés** (A-04). La clé (`Kind`, `Target`, `Context`) reprend celle du registre ; une image et un dépôt ne sont pas la même cible (pas de pont) ; cas résiduels : images sans tag, références écrites autrement. Quels types d'opération le mémorisateur garde-t-il (scan seulement, ou aussi sync, clone, pull, create, delete) ? La table de A-04 (critère 9) est indicative de l'architect.
3. **Vues hors inventaire** (A-00) : **close le 2026-11-06.** Filebrowser, remédiation `:sec` et sessions `:agent-usage` : hors lot, accepté. Vues « sans objet » (dashboard, status, viewer, setup, auth forge, etc.) : acceptées. Le navigateur de registre OCI est sorti de A-09a vers A-09a2 (8e colonne, DEVDESK-218).
4. **Netdiag : échec de test réseau** (A-12) : résultat de ligne (recommandation du PM et de l'architect) ou échec d'opération mémorisé ?
5. **Découpage des PR** : une PR par story (recommandation du PM et de l'architect, avec A-08 et A-09a qui se relisent mieux ensemble mais restent deux PR) ou regroupement des vues Should ?
6. **Quand clore DEVDESK-99.** La décision D11 dit « à la création du backlog » ; question gardée à la demande de l'utilisateur, à confirmer ou à retirer.
7. **Confirmation du réglage dans `:cfg`.** La phrase « or in :cfg » de la légende (A-01) et les critères 4 et 7 de A-02 supposent que `app.motion` est modifiable dans la vue de configuration (champ cyclique `←→`, Rule 132, comme `app.gauge_glyph`). À vérifier par l'architect ; sinon retirer la phrase.
   **Résolu (2026-11-07, DEVDESK-141)** : le réglage est exposé dans `:cfg` (champ cyclique `←→`, onglet `app`) en plus du YAML ; une clé absente reste absente tant qu'on ne cycle pas. La phrase est conservée.
8. **Test de contraste.** Les rapports de `ux.md` §2.1 (au moins 3:1 pour chaque alias sur le fond et sur la ligne sélectionnée) sont des calculs à la main sur les valeurs Catppuccin par défaut ; le test de A-01 (critère 7) doit les confirmer pour chaque thème livré.

Note de méthode : `research.md` ne contient pas de section de critique distincte de la recherche ; les risques de `brief.md` viennent de la liste transmise avec l'idée et des conclusions de la recherche.

---

## Faisabilité (architect)

**Annexe conservée telle quelle (analyse de l'architect). Statut au 2026-11-06 : les révisions d'efforts, de découpage et de fusion sont intégrées au corps des stories et à l'ordre de livraison ci-dessus ; les décisions D1 à D11 tranchent les points marqués « TRANCHÉ » ci-dessous, et les stories font foi en cas d'écart.** Les efforts de la colonne « PM » et les stories A-15, A-07a, A-07b, A-09, A-10 citées ci-dessous n'existent plus telles quelles.

Revue rapide du 2026-11-06, sur `main` à `7cd8ce7`. Pas de plan d'implémentation détaillé ni d'ADR à ce stade. **Verdict : faisable**, à quatre conditions : (1) trancher la contradiction « pas de nouvelle colonne » (R1) **[TRANCHÉ, D1 : option A]** ; (2) reformuler le critère de succès 5 (R2) **[TRANCHÉ, D2]** ; (3) donner au routeur un moyen de savoir qu'une vue veut faire clignoter une ligne hors registre (R3) **[intégré à A-03, critère 6]** ; (4) placer le mémorisateur dans `internal/jobs.Registry` plutôt qu'à côté (R5) **[intégré à A-04, critère 1]**.

### Constats du code (base des estimations)

- **La chaîne D5 existe déjà et tourne à 10 Hz** (`jobSpinnerInterval = spinner.Dot.FPS`, `internal/app/jobs.go`). Elle sert deux lecteurs : la frame nue mise dans les cellules (`ws` Scanned / Git Status, `:sec` Scanned, OCI Scanned et ID, arbre de l'explorer, `:jobs`) et la frame stylée des footers (`RenderedFrame` : `ws`, clone, templates, filebrowser). Chaque tick diffuse un `jobs.ChangedMsg` complet (copie du registre) à toutes les vues tenues, et les vues qui portent la frame dans leurs lignes les reconstruisent à chaque tick.
- **`datatable` a un second mécanisme de spinner par ligne**, `busy` / `StatusColumn` / `AdvanceSpinner`, pour les actions instantanées hors registre : containers (stop, kill, remove), OCI (4 tables : remove, login, logout), netdiag ports (kill). Il est animé par la chaîne locale de chaque vue (le `spinner.TickMsg` de containers et d'OCI, `portsSpinnerCmd` dans ports). C'est une seconde famille de chaînes de ligne, hors D5.
- **Au moins 13 chaînes `spinner.TickMsg` locales** servent le chargement global au footer (containers, netdiag, interfaces, OCI, browser OCI, security, explorer, auth, agent-usage, status, setup, viewer, plus `components`). Le brief les garde, à raison.
- **Première colonne actuelle** (base de R1) :

| Vue / table | 1re colonne | Activité par ligne aujourd'hui | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:jobs` (runs, cibles) | glyphe d'état, `IconColumnWidth` | frame D5 dans le glyphe | registre |
| `ws` | icône fichier, dossier ou dépôt | frame D5 dans Scanned et Git Status | registre (scan, sync, delete) |
| `:sec` inventaire | icône dépôt ou image | frame D5 dans Scanned ; `scanTarget.Failed` | registre (scan) + copie locale |
| explorer (arbre) | icône | frame D5 dans la cellule d'icône | registre (create, delete) + chargement local |
| templates | icône | aucune (footer et touches grisées) | registre (scan, sync) |
| containers | glyphe d'état docker | `busy` + chaîne de la vue | calculé + `busy` |
| filebrowser (hors liste) | icône | aucune (delete au footer) | registre (delete) |
| OCI images | **ID (14 cellules), pas d'icône** | frame D5 dans Scanned et ID (pull) ; `busy` (remove) ; `failedScans` | registre (scan, pull) + `busy` + copie |
| OCI networks, volumes, registries | **texte, pas d'icône** | `busy` + chaîne de la vue | `busy` |
| clone list | **Repository, pas d'icône** | colonne Status, 5 états | registre (clone, run ouverte) |
| netdiag ports | **Proto, pas d'icône** | `busy` (kill) + `portsSpinnerCmd` | `busy` |

| # | Gravité | Risque | Ce qui est faisable / atténuation |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | **Bloquant** | **« Pas de nouvelle colonne » est impossible à tenir** pour OCI (4 tables), la clone list, les ports et `:agent-usage` : aucune n'a de colonne d'icône (tableau ci-dessus). Les mettre en première colonne coûte 4 cellules rendues (2 + rembourrage). À 60 colonnes, des colonnes `Optional` tombent plus tôt, et les seuils documentés (Breakdown « visible dès 106 colonnes ») bougent. | Option A (recommandée) : accepter une colonne de pastille pour ces 7 tables, écrite comme exception au non-objectif. Option B : mettre la pastille dans une cellule existante (2 premières cellules de l'ID d'OCI, colonne State des ports), ce qui casse la forme de la Rule 125 et que le garde-fou A-16 ne peut plus vérifier. Option C : ne migrer que les vues qui ont une colonne d'icône. **Décision de l'utilisateur.** |
| R2 | **Bloquant (critère)** | Le critère de succès 5, « un seul tick d'animation dans l'application », est faux tel qu'écrit : les spinners de chargement du footer gardent leurs 13 chaînes locales, et la chaîne D5 nourrit aussi le spinner du footer des jobs à 10 Hz. | Faisable : **un seul tick anime les lignes**. On fusionne le clignotement dans la chaîne D5 du routeur (voir §3, Q1) ; les chaînes de chargement du footer restent hors périmètre. Le test garde-fou couvre : (a) aucun `tea.Tick` produisant un message d'animation de ligne hors de `internal/app` ; (b) aucun appel à `AdvanceSpinner`, aucun `StatusColumn:` et aucun champ `SpinnerFrame` ou `frame` lu par un `Cell` dans une vue migrée ; (c) `portsSpinnerCmd` supprimé ; (d) avec « sans mouvement », `ensureTick` renvoie `nil` quand seules des pastilles sont en cours. Reformuler le critère 5 dans le brief (PM). |
| R3 | Élevée | **Le routeur ne sait pas qu'une vue veut faire clignoter une ligne hors registre** : `busy` des actions instantanées, agent `running`, chargement des enfants d'un groupe, éventuellement conteneur `restarting`. Aujourd'hui le tick ne vit que si `jobs.Running() > 0`. Un signal par front (une vue envoie « je commence » / « j'ai fini ») reproduit le défaut que D5 a corrigé : une chaîne morte que rien ne relance. | Signal par niveau : interface optionnelle `BlinkingView { WantsBlink() bool }`, sur le modèle de `FormView` et `LeavingView`. Le routeur l'interroge sur les vues tenues **à la fin de chaque `Update`**, puis appelle `ensureTick`. Coût : au plus 16 assertions de type par message. Cela demande d'envelopper `App.Update` (un `update` interne plus un appel final), ce qui change sa structure : à faire dans A-03 et à tester avec `go test -race`. |
| R4 | Élevée | **Composant à deux sources dans `datatable`** : étendre ou remplacer `StatusColumn` et `busy` ? Remplacer d'un coup casse containers, OCI et ports avant leur migration. | **Étendre** : nouveau champ `Column.Indicator func(T) indicator.State`, rendu par `rowLine` avec la phase lue au rendu (`SetBlinkPhase(on bool)`, sans reconstruire ni remesurer : largeur fixe). La précédence `busy` (action instantanée locale) > état fourni par la vue est écrite **une fois** dans `datatable`. L'état fourni par la vue est lui-même construit par **un** helper partagé, `indicator.Resolve(running, queued bool, failure *jobs.Failure, observed indicator.State)`. `StatusColumn`, `AdvanceSpinner` et `spinnerFrame` restent jusqu'à la dernière migration, puis sont supprimés (A-16, critère 7). |
| R5 | Moyenne | **Mémorisateur central** : s'il est tenu à côté du registre, il faut synchroniser deux structures ; s'il est tiré des runs, il perd ses échecs à l'élagage (`MaxFinishedRuns`). | Le mettre **dans `jobs.Registry`**, mis à jour dans `Start` (les cibles admises effacent leur clé) et dans `Apply` (`failed` pose la clé avec `Detail` ; `done` l'efface). On n'y écrit que depuis l'`Update` du routeur, comme pour le reste du registre (Rule 110), et la copie voyage dans `ChangedMsg.Failures`. Ajouter `jobs.ForgetTargetMsg{Target}`, envoyé par une vue à la suppression d'une cible hors registre (remove d'une image), et effacer la clé au `delete` `done` du registre. Hypothèse : plafond de 500 clés, les plus anciennes sortent d'abord (en mémoire, sans disque). |
| R6 | Moyenne | **Identité de cible entre vues** (H4). | Le code la donne déjà : `Item.Target` est la clé du cache de scan. Un dépôt a son chemin absolu en `ws` et dans `:sec` ; une image a sa référence brute (`img.Name()`, `repo:tag`) dans OCI et dans `:sec`. La clé reste celle du registre, (`Kind`, `Target`, `Run.Context`), avec `filepath.Clean` sur les chemins au lancement. Risque résiduel : les images sans tag (`<none>`) et les références écrites autrement (`nginx` contre `docker.io/library/nginx`). À couvrir par un test de clé commune dans A-04 ; pas de spike séparé. |
| R7 | Moyenne | **Recalage des tests de largeur** : ajouter une colonne (R1) change les tests de la Rule 116 et les seuils écrits dans `agent-usage.md`, `network.md`, etc. | Compté dans les efforts de A-09a, A-10b, A-12 et A-13. Le test à 60 colonnes de A-16 doit passer par `RenderedWidth()`, jamais par la somme des colonnes déclarées (Rule 116). |
| R8 | Faible (gain) | **Coût de redessin** (H2). | Le coût **baisse** : aujourd'hui, quand un job tourne, chaque tick à 10 Hz copie le registre et reconstruit les lignes de toutes les vues tenues. Une fois la frame sortie des `Cell`, une phase qui change ne reconstruit rien (lecture au rendu) ; il suffit d'envoyer la phase à la vue à l'écran, plus la phase courante à l'entrée (`switchView`). Le renderer de Bubble Tea ne réécrit que les lignes modifiées, donc une ligne par pastille clignotante sur SSH. A-03 doit séparer « la frame ou la phase a bougé » (`jobs.FrameMsg`, sans snapshot) de « le registre a changé » (`ChangedMsg`). |
| R9 | Faible | **Garde-fous existants**. | `TestAnIconColumnIsUntitledAndTwoCellsWide` passe tel quel si la colonne de pastille est construite par un constructeur de `datatable` (littéral interne avec `IconColumnWidth` nu, déjà accepté) ; il ne voit pas les appels, d'où le test runtime de A-16. `TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` n'est pas touché (il vise les corps, pas les lignes) ; ne pas y greffer A-16. `TestNoShortcutAdvertisesAGlyphAsAKey` reste valable. `TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` doit passer à chaque PR de migration. |
| R10 | Faible | **Phase testable**. | La phase se calcule à partir de l'heure portée par le message de tick (`on = (t.UnixMilli() / 500) % 2 == 0`), pas d'un compteur. Elle survit donc à un changement de cadence et un test l'injecte. L'intervalle reste une `var` (précédent `jobSpinnerInterval`, `testutil.FastTimers`). Tests : rendu `SetBlinkPhase(true/false)` sur une ligne ; arrêt de la chaîne quand le registre est vide et qu'aucune vue ne demande de clignotement ; pas de chaîne avec « sans mouvement » ; numéro de séquence (chaîne remplacée ignorée). |

24	// portsTickMsg triggers a data refresh cycle.
25	type portsTickMsg struct{}

27	// portsDataMsg carries the result of a socket-table read.
28	type portsDataMsg struct {
29		ports []ports.Socket
30		err   error
31	}
32	
33	// portsKillResultMsg carries the result of a kill.
34	type portsKillResultMsg struct {
35		pid string
36		err error
37	}
38	
39	// portsSpinnerTickMsg turns the frame of a row a kill is running on.
40	//
41	// This model has no spinner of its own, and its data tick is two seconds apart
42	// — a frame that advanced on that would look stopped, which is the impression
43	// the whole thing exists to remove. So the kill starts a tick of its own and it
44	// stops itself when nothing is left running.
45	type portsSpinnerTickMsg struct{}
46	
47	func portsSpinnerCmd() tea.Cmd {
48		return tea.Tick(spinner.Dot.FPS, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return portsSpinnerTickMsg{} })
49	}
50	
51	// defaultPortsRefresh is what the interval falls back to. A non-positive one —
52	// a hand-edited 0 in the config — would make tea.Tick fire without pausing and
53	// spin a docker exec per frame, so it is refused here rather than trusted.
54	const defaultPortsRefresh = 2 * time.Second
55	
56	func portsTickCmd(every time.Duration) tea.Cmd {
57		if every <= 0 {
58			every = defaultPortsRefresh
59		}
60		return tea.Tick(every, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
61			return portsTickMsg{}
62		})
63	}
64	
65	// portsFetchTimeout bounds one read. Reverse DNS is the part that can hang —
66	// the socket table itself is a system call — and a fetch outliving several
67	// ticks would stack one behind another.
68	const portsFetchTimeout = 5 * time.Second
69	
70	func fetchPortsCmd(numeric bool) tea.Cmd {
71		return func() tea.Msg {
72			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), portsFetchTimeout)
73			defer cancel()
74			sockets, err := ports.List(ctx, !numeric)
75			return portsDataMsg{ports: sockets, err: err}
76		}
77	}
78	
79	func killProcessCmd(pid string) tea.Cmd {
80		return func() tea.Msg {
81			return portsKillResultMsg{pid: pid, err: ports.Kill(pid)}
82		}
83	}
84	
85	// statusLine is what the Ports tab derives on every frame. Pausing is a state
86	// rather than an event, so it is rendered from pm.paused instead of set as a
87	// message — a message would expire after three seconds while still paused.
88	func (pm *PortsModel) statusLine() components.Status {
89		// Staleness outranks the pause: a pause is what the user asked for, an
90		// unreachable Docker is not, and only one of the two makes the rows lie.
91		if pm.stale {
92			return components.Status{Text: pm.staleLabel(), Level: components.LevelError}
93		}
94		if pm.paused {
95			return components.Status{Text: "Paused — press space to resume"}
96		}
97		return components.Status{}

100	// staleLabel dates the rows on screen, or says there are none to date.
101	func (pm *PortsModel) staleLabel() string {
102		if pm.lastOK.IsZero() {
103			return "The socket table could not be read"
104		}
105		return "The socket table could not be read — ports as of " + theme.TimeAgo(pm.lastOK)
106	}

108	// filterTokenProto and filterTokenState are the label constants for FilterBar tokens.
109	const (
110		filterTokenTCP     = "tcp"
111		filterTokenUDP     = "udp"
112		filterTokenListen  = "LISTEN"
113		filterTokenEstab   = "ESTAB"
114		filterTokenPaused  = "⏸ PAUSED"
115		filterTokenNumeric = "numeric"
116	)

118	// PortsModel manages the real-time port monitoring sub-view.
119	type PortsModel struct {
120		// refresh is how often the table re-reads the socket table. The spinner tick is separate
121		// and much faster: a frame advancing on this interval would look stopped,
122		// which is the impression the whole tab exists to remove.
123		refresh time.Duration
124		width   int
125		height  int
126	
127		// The table holds the entries, filters them and keeps the cursor. The
128		// tableReady / lastTableWidth / lastTableHeight trio that used to live here
129		// existed only to avoid recreating the table on every two-second tick and
130		// losing the scroll position; SetItems guarantees that instead.
131		table datatable.Model[ports.Socket]
132	
133		paused bool
134	
135		// address display
136		// numericAddrs true shows addresses as the system reports them; false asks
137		// reverse DNS for the host half. The port half stays numeric either way —
138		// resolving it to a service name would be DevDesk guessing where `ss` read
139		// /etc/services, and saying less beats saying something the system did not.
140		numericAddrs bool
141	
142		// confirmModal guards the kill. It is the only action in the application
143		// that reaches a process outside it, so it is the one that most needed a
144		// confirmation and had none.
145		confirmModal *components.ConfirmModal
146	
147		// lastOK is when the table last received real data, and stale says the most
148		// recent fetch failed.
149		//
150		// They exist because a failed fetch keeps the rows: dropping them would
151		// flash the table empty on a transient hiccup, two seconds apart, and the
152		// rows are not wrong — they are dated. What was missing is their age. A
153		// footer *message* cannot carry it either: it expires after three seconds
154		// (Rule 128), and what was left was a table refreshing into failure with
155		// nothing on screen saying so. That is D20's shape — "we could not look"
156		// rendered as data.

172			return datatable.Column[ports.Socket]{Sizing: sizing, Cell: get, Search: get}

197	// scanned down: a listening port is something the machine offers, an
198	// established one is a conversation in progress, and everything else is a
199	// socket on its way out.
200	func portStateStyle(p ports.Socket) lipgloss.Style {
201		switch strings.ToUpper(p.State) {
202		case "LISTEN":
203			return theme.StatusOKStyle
204		case "ESTAB", "ESTABLISHED":

213	// matchPortTokens applies the toggle filters: OR within a group, AND between
214	// them. `numeric` and `paused` are shown in the bar but filter nothing — they
215	// report a mode, which is why they are not consulted here.
216	func matchPortTokens(p ports.Socket, active map[string]bool) bool {
217		return matchesActive(p.Protocol, active, filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP) &&
218			matchesActive(p.State, active, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab)

222	// on. A group with nothing on does not filter: that is "no opinion", not
223	// "match nothing", and getting the two confused would empty the table on open.
224	func matchesActive(value string, active map[string]bool, labels ...string) bool {
225		anyOn := false
226		for _, label := range labels {
227			if !active[label] {
228				continue
229			}
230			anyOn = true
231			if strings.EqualFold(value, label) {
232				return true
233			}
234		}
235		return !anyOn

238	// newPortsModel creates a new PortsModel.

278		pm.width = width
279		pm.height = height
280		if width == 0 {
281			return

288	func (pm *PortsModel) update(msg tea.Msg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
289		switch msg := msg.(type) {
290		case portsTickMsg:
291			return pm.handleTick()
292		case portsDataMsg:
293			return pm.handleData(msg)
294		case portsKillResultMsg:
295			return pm.handleKillResult(msg)
296		case portsSpinnerTickMsg:
297			return pm.handleSpinnerTick()
298		case components.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
299			pm.confirmModal = nil
300			return pm.killSelected()
301		case components.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
302			pm.confirmModal = nil
303			return pm, nil
304		case tea.KeyMsg:
305			return pm.handleKey(msg)
306		}
307		return pm, nil
308	}
309	
310	// handleSpinnerTick advances the frame and schedules the next one, or lets the
311	// tick die when the last kill has landed.
312	func (pm *PortsModel) handleSpinnerTick() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
313		if len(pm.table.BusyLabels()) == 0 {
314			return pm, nil
315		}
316		pm.table.AdvanceSpinner()
317		return pm, portsSpinnerCmd()
318	}
319	
320	func (pm *PortsModel) handleTick() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
321		if pm.paused {
322			return pm, portsTickCmd(pm.refresh)
323		}
324		return pm, tea.Batch(fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs), portsTickCmd(pm.refresh))
325	}
326	
327	func (pm *PortsModel) handleData(msg portsDataMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
328		if msg.err != nil {
329			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.List: %v", msg.err)
330			// The rows stay: they are dated, not wrong, and the status line is what
331			// says so. No footer message — this is a state, and a state that
332			// expires after three seconds is how a dead table came to look alive.
333			pm.stale = true
334			return pm, nil
335		}
336		pm.stale = false
337		pm.lastOK = time.Now()
338		// The cursor and the scroll survive this, which is what the whole
339		// tableReady dance existed to achieve on a two-second tick.
340		pm.table.SetItems(msg.ports)
341		return pm, nil
342	}
343	
344	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKillResult(msg portsKillResultMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
345		// On every outcome: a kill that failed has to let the socket state show
346		// again rather than go on turning.
347		pm.table.ClearBusy(msg.pid)
348		if msg.err != nil {
349			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.Kill pid=%s: %v", msg.pid, msg.err)
350			return pm, pm.footer.Error(killFailureMessage(msg.pid, msg.err))
351		}
352		return pm, pm.footer.Info(fmt.Sprintf("Process %s terminated", msg.pid))
353	}
354	
355	// killFailureMessage says why the signal did not land.
356	//
357	// DevDesk signals with the rights it has (§3.43), so the refusal the user meets
358	// most often is the operating system's — another user's process, a service, one
359	// Windows protects. "Failed to kill PID 1234" gave them no reason to suspect
360	// that, and made "access denied" and "already gone" the same sentence.
361	//
362	// The platform error itself never reaches the screen: it comes back in the
363	// machine's own language — measured here, PID 4 answers `OpenProcess: Accès
364	// refusé.` — which is the route stage's rule (§3.44). errors.Is reads through
365	// the %w wrapping ports.Kill applies, and both sentinels are the standard
366	// library's.
367	//
368	// The permission branch was measured on Windows: killing PID 4 (System) gives
369	// ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, which syscall.Errno maps onto os.ErrPermission. EPERM
370	// maps the same way on Unix.
371	//
372	// **The "already gone" branch does not fire on Windows**, and that is measured
373	// too: a PID that does not exist fails OpenProcess with
374	// ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which maps to neither sentinel, so it falls to the
375	// generic message. Mapping that code would be a guess — it is what an invalid
376	// argument returns as well — and the row disappears on the next two-second
377	// refresh anyway. The branch is kept because ESRCH does map to
378	// os.ErrProcessDone on Unix.
379	func killFailureMessage(pid string, err error) string {
380		switch {
381		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
382			return fmt.Sprintf("Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID %s", pid)
383		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrProcessDone):
384			return fmt.Sprintf("PID %s is no longer running", pid)
385		}
386		return fmt.Sprintf("Failed to kill PID %s — check logs", pid)
387	}
388	
389	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
390		if pm.confirmModal != nil {
391			var cmd tea.Cmd
392			pm.confirmModal, cmd = pm.confirmModal.Update(msg)
393			return pm, cmd
394		}
395		if pm.table.InEditMode() {
396			cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
397			pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
398			return pm, cmd
399		}
400		return pm.handleKeyNormal(msg)
401	}
402	
403	// toggleToken flips a filter and returns to the top, since the list under the
404	// cursor is not the list the user was looking at any more.
405	func (pm *PortsModel) toggleToken(label string) {
406		pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, !pm.table.IsTokenActive(label))
407		pm.table.GotoTop()
408	}
409	
410	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKeyNormal(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
411		switch msg.String() {
412		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end", "/":
413			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
414		case " ":
415			pm.paused = !pm.paused
416			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenPaused, pm.paused)
417			// Pausing is a state, not an event: it is derived in statusLine rather
418			// than set as a message, which would expire while still paused.
419		case "t":
420			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenTCP)
421		case "u":
422			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenUDP)
423		case "l":
424			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenListen)
425		case "e":
426			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenEstab)
427		case "n":
428			pm.numericAddrs = !pm.numericAddrs
429			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenNumeric, pm.numericAddrs)
430			return pm, fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)
431		case "z":
432			for _, label := range []string{
433				filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab, filterTokenPaused,
434			} {
435				pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, false)
436			}
437			pm.table.FilterBar().ClearSearch()
438			pm.table.SetItems(pm.table.Items()) // re-apply with the query gone
439			pm.paused = false
440			pm.table.GotoTop()
441		case keymap.Kill:
442			return pm.confirmKill()
443		}
444		return pm, nil
445	}
446	
447	// confirmKill asks before sending the signal.
448	//
449	// This is the one action in the application that reaches outside it: not a
450	// container to be brought back up, but a process belonging to whoever is at
451	// this machine, killed with SIGKILL so it gets no chance to save anything. It
452	// had no confirmation at all, while deleting a container — recreatable from its
453	// image — had one (§3.26).
454	func (pm *PortsModel) confirmKill() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
455		if k := pm.killable(); !k.Enabled() {
456			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(k.Reason)
457		}
458		entry, _ := pm.table.Selected()
459		if pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
460			return pm, pm.footer.Warn("Already killing PID " + entry.PID)
461		}
462		pm.confirmModal = components.NewConfirmModal(
463			"Kill Process",
464			fmt.Sprintf("Send SIGKILL to %s (PID %s)?\n\nThe process gets no chance to shut down cleanly.",
465				entry.Process, entry.PID),
466		)
467		return pm, nil
468	}
469	
470	// Why K does not apply, written once so the header, the footer and the tests
471	// cannot drift apart on the wording (Rule 129 — English US).
472	const (
473		reasonNoSocketRow = "No socket selected"
474		reasonNoPID       = "The system did not say which process holds this socket"
475	)
476	
477	// killable reports whether K has a process to signal (Rule 130).
478	//
479	// A socket the system declines to attribute carries no PID — `List` blanks a
480	// PID of zero rather than printing it, because process 0 is a whole process
481	// group on Unix and a row reading "0" would look killable. That is the state
482	// this greys; whether the operating system will *accept* the signal is a
483	// different question, and one only the attempt can answer.
484	func (pm *PortsModel) killable() shortcut.Availability {
485		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
486		switch {
487		case !ok:
488			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoSocketRow)
489		case entry.PID == "":
490			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoPID)
491		}
492		return shortcut.Availability{}
493	}
494	
495	// killSelected sends the signal, once confirmed.
496	func (pm *PortsModel) killSelected() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
497		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
498		if !ok {
499			return pm, nil
500		}
501		if entry.PID == "" || pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
502			return pm, nil
503		}
504		// Keyed on the PID, so every socket the process holds spins at once — which
505		// is what happens: the kill takes them all. The State cell is the one to
506		// spend, being exactly what the signal is about to change.
507		pm.table.MarkBusy(entry.PID, "Killing "+entry.Process+" ("+entry.PID+")")
508		return pm, tea.Batch(killProcessCmd(entry.PID), portsSpinnerCmd())
509	}
510	
511	// view renders the table. An empty table stays a table (Rule 139) — its
512	// header and no rows — whether it is genuinely empty, filtered down to
513	// nothing, still loading, or stale: those are a footer status (statusLine) and
514	// a header count, never body text.
515	func (pm *PortsModel) view() string {
516		return pm.table.View()
517	}
518	
519	// summaryLine counts what is on screen, for the header (Rule 139).
520	func (pm *PortsModel) summaryLine() string {
521		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(pm.table.Items()))
522	}
523
